league.t: In each of Weeks 1 through 13, the franchise with the lowest score pays $50 into the penalty pool. That money buys bitcoin, which is held separately from the luxury pool. The fine is called out in the Dispatch and on the home page every week.
The penalty pool is paid out after Week 14. Half goes to the team with the most points in the whole league that week. A quarter goes to the team with the second-most.
The last quarter of the pool goes to the team with the highest single-week score from Weeks 1 through 13. The current record holder is shown on the home page, and every new record is announced.

moves.t: During the season, players are added through free agency or through blind-bid waivers. Which one applies depends on the day and on whether the player’s game has started.
Free agency opens every Thursday at 9 a.m. ET. Until a player’s NFL game kicks off that week, anyone can add or drop him, and the move goes through right away.
At kickoff of his NFL game, a player locks for the rest of the week. From then until waivers run, he can only be added with a blind-bid waiver claim.
Waivers run every Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET. Each claim includes a bid from the team’s budget, and the highest bid wins the player. The site prompts for a bid whenever an add falls inside the lock.

playoffs.t: Eight teams make the playoffs. Six spots are set when the regular season ends after Week 13. The last two are decided in Week 14.
The three division winners get in automatically. A division is won by the best overall record in it. If records are tied, the team with more total season points wins the division.
The three teams with the best records among the non-division-winners also get in, using the same total-points tiebreaker. Seeds 1 through 6 are now set.
The teams ranked 7th through 10th after Week 13 play one week against each other at once. Head-to-head results don't count. Only each team's total score matters.
Points are added to Week 14 scores based on rank after Week 13. The 7th-place team gets 100 points and the 8th-place team gets 50. The 9th- and 10th-place teams start from zero.
The two highest Free-For-All scores, head start included, take the 7 and 8 seeds. Whichever of the two scores higher is the 7 seed.
Before the first round, the three division winners each choose their opponent from the other playoff teams. The 1 seed picks first, then the 2 seed, then the 3 seed.
The two teams nobody picks play each other in the first round. For the rest of the playoffs, those two are the 4 and 5 seeds.
The four first-round winners move on to the semifinals. The highest remaining seed picks its opponent, and the other two teams play each other.
